summary: Reviewed the exact base-to-head diff of `src/host/target-tree-facts.ts`, `tests/host/target-tree-facts_test.ts` and `tests/host/targets_test.ts`. The resolver now proves the default-branch head with one `/commits/{branch}` read per lookup, then reuses SHA-pinned facts from a process-wide cache keyed by API base, credential, owner and name; null and refused resolutions are evicted so they retry, concurrent callers share one in-flight promise, and workflow scans are capped with an unproven remainder returning null rather than a defaulted policy. The added tests cover concurrent reuse, recreated resolvers and transports, SHA changes, credential/base isolation, unavailable heads, retry-after-failure, gateway/self targets and the 27-target reload lifecycle, and the existing `treeFactsHttp` fixture updates keep the branch-pinned targets tests valid. No actionable defect introduced by this change was found.

evidence: `src/host/target-tree-facts.ts:57-60` and `:323-356` add a process-scoped facts cache keyed by API base, token, owner and name; every lookup still performs a `/commits/{defaultBranch}` head read and reuses only facts resolved for that exact 40-hex SHA, deleting null or refused entries so they retry.

`src/host/target-tree-facts.ts:50` and `:234-247` bound workflow file reads to `MAX_WORKFLOW_FILES = 10` and return null when the workflow listing exceeds the read budget, so the scan can no longer be unbounded or silently default to a no-CI policy.

`tests/host/target-tree-facts_test.ts:260-313` proves the 27-target config reload lifecycle reuses cached facts (108 contents reads, unchanged on reload), re-reads on a new default-branch SHA (216) and returns zero configs when the head is unavailable.

`ops/hosted-autonomy-matrix-adapters.ts:93-109` and `src/host/targets.ts:299-338` still send every generic target through the resolver on each load, so the SHA-keyed cache is what removes the repeated root listing, manifest and workflow reads.
